name: Push to Transcribe
description: Dictate into any app without leaving it, with an optional LLM pass that cleans up the transcript before pasting.

intelligence.tagline: macOS menu bar app that turns held-Caps-Lock speech into pasted text
gettingStarted: Run ./scripts/build_app.sh — it compiles, bundles, installs to /Applications, and launches the app.
Click the menu bar mic icon → Settings… → API Key and paste an OpenAI API key (stored in the macOS Keychain, not in a file).
Grant Microphone and Accessibility permissions when prompted (System Settings → Privacy & Security).
Hold Caps Lock to record, release to transcribe and auto-paste; hold Option+Space to also run an LLM cleanup pass.
Run ./scripts/build_and_export.sh to produce exports/PushToTranscribe.dmg for another Mac.
intelligence.deploySummary: Ships as an ad-hoc-signed DMG built on this Mac by scripts/build_and_export.sh — no CI, no notarization, no App Store.

architecture.pattern: single-target AppKit app with an AppDelegate coordinator wiring seven single-responsibility manager classes
architecture.apiStyle: outbound REST calls to the OpenAI API; the app exposes no server or IPC surface
architecture.stateManagement: SettingsManager as an ObservableObject with @Published properties that persist on didSet; closure callbacks (onHotkeyPressed, onTranscriptionComplete, onAPIError) between managers
architecture.dataFlow: Caps Lock down (CGEvent tap) -> AudioRecordingManager taps AVAudioEngine input -> AVAudioConverter resamples to 16kHz mono 16-bit PCM -> buffered in WhisperClient -> key up -> WAV header prepended -> multipart POST to OpenAI transcriptions -> optional LLMClient cleanup pass -> ClipboardUtils copies and synthesizes Cmd+V into the previously focused app
architecture.a11y: SF Symbols carry accessibilityDescription; app requests Accessibility (AX) permission for hotkeys and synthetic paste

notable.name: (none)
notable.purpose: Package.swift declares zero external dependencies — everything is Apple system frameworks, which is why there is no lockfile and builds are fully offline

structure.licenseType: README claims MIT but no LICENSE file exists in the repo

DEAD CODE — leftover from the old MacWhisper target, not referenced by any target in Package.swift

security.secretsManagement: OpenAI API key lives in the macOS Keychain (kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked); no .env files, nothing secret in the repo. Keys are masked to prefix+suffix in all log output.
security.inputValidation: none — no user-supplied input crosses a trust boundary; API responses are parsed defensively with guard/optional chaining
notes: Entitlements are broad for an ad-hoc-signed local app: allow-jit, allow-unsigned-executable-memory, disable-library-validation, network.client and network.server.
The app takes a CGEvent tap and synthesizes keystrokes, so it requires full Accessibility trust — a high-privilege grant on macOS.

Every recording is archived to disk in cleartext (WAV + transcript) under ~/Library/Application Support/PushToTranscribe/voice-archive with no retention limit, which contradicts the README's 'No Storage' claim.
Bundle identifier is still the placeholder com.example.pushtotranscribe, which is also the Keychain service name and keychain-access-group.

conventions.codeStyle: class-based Swift with 4-space indent, MARK: section comments, [weak self] in every escaping closure, DispatchQueue.main.async before touching UI, emoji-prefixed print/log lines
conventions.namingConvention: PascalCase types, camelCase members, manager classes suffixed -Manager, network callers suffixed -Client, stateless helpers as enums or -Utils
conventions.commitConvention: none — short freeform imperative subjects ('Working', 'Updates', 'Update model')
conventions.branchStrategy: single main branch, committed directly, no feature branches in history

agentNotes: There is no test suite, no linter, and no CI. The only verification loop is `swift build --configuration release` followed by launching the app and exercising the hotkey by hand.

The build's Info.plist source of truth is `MacWhisper.app/Contents/Info.plist` — both build scripts copy it into the new bundle. Despite `*.app/` in .gitignore this file IS tracked in git. Edit bundle metadata (version, usage strings, LSUIElement) there, not in PushToTranscribe.app/, which build_and_export.sh deletes when it finishes.
`Sources/MacWhisper/AudioRecordingManager.swift` is dead code — Package.swift only builds the PushToTranscribe target from Sources/PushToTranscribe. Do not edit it expecting an effect.

The README is stale: it describes the old MacWhisper app name, a Control+Space default hotkey, an API key hardcoded in AppDelegate, and 1-second chunked streaming. Reality is Caps Lock push-to-talk, a Keychain-stored key set in Settings, and one upload of the whole utterance on key release. `scripts/run.sh` and `scripts/test_hotkeys.sh` still point at MacWhisper paths that no longer exist and will fail.

Caps Lock push-to-talk works by remapping Caps Lock to F18 at the HID level (CapsLockHIDRemap.apply). This is a SYSTEM-WIDE change. The app restores it in applicationWillTerminate, but a crash or force-quit leaves Caps Lock dead — run the 'Restore Caps Lock' script (`hidutil property --set '{"UserKeyMapping":[]}'`) to fix it.

After each rebuild macOS often invalidates the Accessibility grant because the executable changed. If hotkeys or auto-paste silently stop, remove PushToTranscribe from System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, re-add /Applications/PushToTranscribe.app, and relaunch.

Two hotkeys exist: the primary push-to-talk (default Caps Lock, hold to record) and a cleanup hotkey (default Option+Space) that routes the transcript through LLMClient with a user-editable prompt before pasting.

Transcription model IDs live in three places that must stay in sync: the SettingsManager default, the SettingsView picker tags, and the language-parameter branch in WhisperClient (gpt-transcribe sends `languages` as an array; older models send `language` as a string).

This is a menu bar app (LSUIElement, .accessory policy) with no ports, no server, and no dev server. The one Nomad process runs the installed bundle executable directly so stdout logging is visible; the Diagnostics settings tab shows the same log in-app.

Use the Nomad process log (`nomad proc logs -k <id> -n 80`) to read startup, permission, hotkey-registration, and OpenAI request/response lines — every manager logs through the shared DiagnosticLogger.
